title: Measuring photophysiological traits of diatoms using a Water-PAM
author: Phoebe Argyle

steps.title: Prepare the sample cuvette
steps.instruction: Transfer the microalgae culture into a glass cuvette compatible with the WATER-PAM instrument.

substeps.instruction: Take a 2 mL aliquot of culture.
If total culture volume is <2 mL, take 0.5-1 mL and dilute with sterile seawater to a final volume of 2 mL.
Note: The optimal volume for the WATER-PAM is 2-3 mL.

steps.title: Set up the instrument
steps.instruction: Set up the WATER-PAM (PAM fluorometer, WALZ, WATER-PAM-II) according to the manufacturer's instructions.

steps.title: Initiate Rapid Light Curve (RLC)
steps.instruction: Start the RLC by selecting Program > Light Curve in WinControl.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the curve has at least 3 points on the rise, multiple points to estimate ETRmax, and at least one point on the decline at the highest irradiance.
If criteria are not met, optimize instrument settings such as gain and irradiance steps.
Modify the Light Curve Intensity (LI) to change the first irradiance step (the curve always contains 8 steps).
Set the curve width to 10 seconds.

steps.title: Adjust gain and sample consistency
steps.instruction: Configure gain settings to ensure data quality and comparability.

substeps.instruction: Reduce the gain or dilute the sample if Fo or Fm exceeds the maximum value (>4000).
Do not adjust gain settings between samples to maintain data comparability.
Conduct all measurements for different cultures within a similar time window based on the photoperiod (e.g., within a 1-2 hour window, 2 hours after the onset of light).
